rationale: The assistant immediately issued the correct safety stop ('Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged'), correctly linked the ~15 minute timing to the heating phase, and hedged the diagnosis as 'most likely' the element with an earth leakage fault, escalating to an electrician or appliance engineer for testing. It did not fabricate anything or push a part. Weaknesses: it asked no questions (e.g. water near the socket, whether cold rinse trips), and the suggestion to look for 'cracks in the ceramic parts of the heater element' is of dubious relevance for a dishwasher element, though harmless with the machine unplugged. A UK homeowner would be safely and reasonably well served.
